questions.question: The provision for the post of Vice-President in the Indian Constitution was taken from ________.
questions.solution: The post of Vice-President in India was modeled after the Constitution of the United States of America. Similar to the US Vice President, the Indian Vice-President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Upper House (Rajya Sabha). Note: In the US, the VP succeeds to the presidency for the remainder of the term, whereas in India, the VP only acts as President until a new one is elected.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_2: They can be suspended during an emergency
questions.option_3: They are available against the state
questions.solution: A defining feature of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) is that they are non-justiciable. This means they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation (unlike Fundamental Rights). However, Article 37 clarifies that they are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a political philosophy of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_2: Non-committal to building a common national identity
questions.option_3: Sensitive for the historically disadvantaged groups
questions.option_4: Sensitive to the needs of religious and linguistic minorities
questions.solution: The statement that the Constitution is 'Non-committal to building a common national identity' is NOT a political philosophy of the Indian Constitution. The Constitution actively seeks to promote a common national identity while respecting diversity. Core Philosophies: It is sensitive to disadvantaged groups, protective of minorities, and open to community values through secularism and social justice.

questions.question: Which of the following words is NOT mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The word 'Federalism' is NOT mentioned anywhere in the Indian Constitution. While the Constitution describes the structure of the government as federal, Article 1 simply uses the phrase 'Union of States'. Comparison: Words like Secular, Republic, and Socialist are explicitly mentioned in the Preamble.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: They are enumerated in Part II of the Constitution
questions.option_2: It has been borrowed from the Soviet Union
questions.option_3: It is described as 'a novel feature of the Constitution'
questions.solution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles of State Policy as a 'novel feature of the Constitution'. Corrections: They are in Part IV (not Part II), were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (not Soviet Union), and consist of Articles 36 to 51 (not 12 to 32).

questions.question: In the Indian constitution, the concept of 'equality before law' is borrowed from the ______ constitution.
questions.solution: The concept of 'Equality before Law' is borrowed from the British Constitution (specifically the 'Rule of Law' concept by A.V. Dicey). Distinction: While 'Equality before Law' (negative concept) is British, 'Equal Protection of Laws' (positive concept) is borrowed from the US Constitution. Both are included in Article 14.

questions.question: The original Constitution of India was handwritten in English by:
questions.solution: The original Constitution of India was handwritten in flowing italic calligraphy by Prem Behari Narain Raizada. He took six months to complete the task and did not charge any fee, asking only to sign his name on every page and his grandfather's name on the last page.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities was the chief draftsman of the constituent assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution?
questions.solution: S.N. Mukherjee was the chief draftsman of the Constituent Assembly. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar praised him for his ability to put complex proposals into very clear and concise legal terminology. Note: H.V.R. Iyengar was the Secretary of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question: The idea of the concurrent list in the Indian Constitution was taken from _______.
questions.solution: The idea of the Concurrent List was borrowed from the Constitution of Australia. This list (List III of the 7th Schedule) contains subjects where both the Centre and the States can make laws, though Union law prevails in case of a conflict. Note: The language of the Preamble was also influenced by Australia.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Indian Constitution is the lengthiest written constitution in the world. Corrections: India has Single Citizenship (not dual), is a blend of rigidity and flexibility (not just rigid), and follows a Parliamentary form of government (not presidential).

questions.question: "The Constitution of free India must be framed, without outside interference by a constituent assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise." Who made this statement?
questions.solution: Jawaharlal Nehru made this statement in 1938 while representing the Indian National Congress. He demanded that the Constituent Assembly be elected through adult franchise to ensure the constitution truly reflected the will of the Indian people without British interference.

questions.question: Which of the following is a liberal principle of the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: To secure the right to work
questions.option_2: To secure a uniform civil code
questions.solution: Securing a Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) is categorized as a Liberal-Intellectual principle of the DPSP. Other categories: Socialistic principles (like right to work) and Gandhian principles (like promoting cottage industries). UCC aims to replace diverse personal laws with a common set of laws for all citizens.

questions.question: Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity slogan of __________ finds an echo in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity were borrowed from the French Revolution (1789). These three words in the Preamble symbolize the democratic and social aspirations of the Indian Republic.

questions.question: In India the principle of ‘procedure established by law’ is taken from which constitution?
questions.solution: The principle of 'Procedure established by law' is taken from the Constitution of Japan. It means that a law is valid if it has been passed by the legislature following the correct legal procedure. Note: This is mentioned in Article 21 regarding the protection of life and personal liberty.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote in calligraphic style the Hindi version of the original Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: While the English version was calligraphed by Raizada, the Hindi version of the original Constitution was handwritten by Vasant Krishan Vaidya. Note: Both versions were elegantly decorated and illuminated by artists from Shantiniketan, including Nand Lal Bose.

questions.question: India is a parliamentary democracy based on the 'Westminster' model of _________.
questions.solution: India follows the Westminster model of government, which is the parliamentary system of the United Kingdom. Key features include a nominal head of state (President), a real executive (Prime Minister), and the collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
A) They are negative in nature.
B) They have moral and political sanctions.
C) They promote the welfare of the rich.
D) They are positive in nature.
questions.solution: Statements B and D are correct. Directive Principles are positive in nature as they require the State to do certain things (unlike Fundamental Rights which are often negative/restrictive). They also have moral and political sanctions; while not legally enforceable, no government can ignore them for long without facing the voters. [Image comparing Fundamental Rights and DPSP]

questions.question: Which of the following principles was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife
questions.option_2: Reservation of SC's and ST's in services
questions.option_3: To organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines
questions.option_4: The State shall provide free and compulsory education
questions.solution: Article 48-A, which directs the state 'to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife,' was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment also added Article 39A (Free legal aid) and Article 43A (Workers' participation in management).

questions.question: The structural part of the Indian Constitution is, to a large extent, derived from the Act of _________.
questions.solution: The structural part of the Indian Constitution is largely derived from the Government of India Act, 1935. About 250 provisions of the Constitution are identical to or closely follow this Act, including the Federal Scheme, Office of Governor, Judiciary, and Public Service Commissions.

questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is NOT borrowed from the Canadian constitution?
questions.option_2: Appointment of state governor by the centre
questions.option_4: Advisory jurisdiction of the supreme court
questions.solution: The Concurrent List is NOT borrowed from Canada; it is borrowed from Australia. Canadian Features: Federation with a strong centre, appointment of state governors by the centre, and the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the category of Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: While the DPSP are officially categorized by scholars into Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual principles, there is no 'Nehruvian' category mentioned in standard constitutional studies. Nehru's ideals are largely reflected within the Socialistic and Liberal categories.

questions.question: In India which of the following is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.option_2: To provide equal pay for equal work
questions.solution: The organisation of Village Panchayats (Article 40) is a Gandhian principle. Gandhi believed that India lives in its villages and advocated for 'Gram Swaraj'. Others: Equal pay (Socialistic), UCC (Liberal), and Separation of Judiciary (Liberal).

questions.question:
Match list I with list II and choose your answer from the code below.
List-I List-II
(A) Habeas corpus (i) Enquiring into legality of claim
(B) Mandamus (ii) To command
(C) Quo warranto (iii) To have a body of
(D) Certiorari (iv) To be certified
questions.solution: The correct match is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv. Habeas Corpus (To have the body), Mandamus (We command), Quo Warranto (By what authority/legality of claim), and Certiorari (To be certified/informed). These are the five writs under Articles 32 and 226.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement in regard to the meaning of ‘Union of States” in the Indian context?
questions.option_1: Enumerates the power of centre and states through various lists.
questions.option_2: Country was divided into different states for administrative convenience.
questions.option_3: Indian federation was the result of an agreement by sovereign units to join it.
questions.option_4: Federation not being the result of agreement, no state has a right to secede from it.
questions.solution: The statement that the 'Indian federation was the result of an agreement by sovereign units' is INCORRECT. Unlike the USA, the Indian federation is not a result of an agreement between states, and consequently, no state has the right to secede from the Union. This makes the Union indestructible.

questions.question: Indian Council of Historical Research is a captive body of __________, Government of India.
questions.solution: The Indian Council of Historical Research (ICHR) is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development). It was established to provide an objective and scientific writing of history and to promote historical research.

questions.question: In India, which Act divided the powers between the Central and units in terms of three lists?
questions.solution: The Government of India Act, 1935 was the first to divide powers between the Centre and the units (provinces) through three lists: the Federal List, Provincial List, and Concurrent List. This laid the foundation for the current 7th Schedule of the Constitution.
